  - region "Simple English explanation of Vector Projection":
    - paragraph: In simple English
    - heading "Understand Vector Projection" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "The projection of a onto b is ((a·b)/|b|^2) b. The shadow of <2,2> on <1,0> is <2,0>. The formula uses the unit direction of b. A useful rule is Vector Projection: proj_v u=((u dot v)/(v dot v))v. You can learn Vector Projection by trying one small example instead of long theory."
    - paragraph: "Compute a·b, divide by |b|^2, then multiply that scalar by the vector b. Example: Project (3,4) onto the x-axis. The x-axis keeps horizontal part. Horizontal component is 3. So the answer is (3,0)."
    - paragraph: "In real life, shadows: A shadow is a projection. Watch out: Keeping the whole vector instead of its shadow. Projection keeps only the part along the target vector."
    - complementary:
      - generic: Try this example
      - paragraph: Project (3,4) onto the x-axis.
      - generic "Compare your answer"
